\subsection{Cyclic Propagation in the All-\texorpdfstring{$\Vdzero$}{Vd0} Cases}
\label{sec:cyclic-all-vd0}

\subsubsection{The exactly-one-supercritical all-\texorpdfstring{$\Vdzero$}{Vd0} branch}

For a center interval, call the nonempty closed set missed by its two open
endpoint triangles a \emph{boundary gap}. It may be a singleton. If the maximal
closed center trace is $[s,t]$, open coverage gives the weak bounds
$B_i\ge s$ and $A_{i+1}\ge1-t$; thus none of the arguments below discards a
singleton gap.

\begin{proposition}[CE1 one-gap five-map obstruction]
\label{prop:ce1-one-gap}
\label{thm:s2-geom-r1}
Assume that every V triangle is $\Vdzero$, $N_+=1$, and the C triangle is
CE1. If its boundary trace contains a boundary gap, the triangles do not
cover $H$.
\end{proposition}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 04e_strategy2_verification_03_cyclic_propagation_in_the_all_vdzero_cases.tex).

\begin{proposition}[nonempty gap all-$\Vdzero$, $N_+=1$]
\label{prop:nplus-one-all-vd0}
If the C triangle is CE1 or CE2, every V triangle is $\Vdzero$, and
$N_+=1$, then no cover of $H$ can have a boundary gap in the actual open
V triangle traces.
\end{proposition}
